InDiD stream detector

Source: R/dfr_indid.R
dfr_indid.Rd

Monitors a stream with a trained indid() model: the observations are fed one by one to the recurrent network, and a drift is reported when the probability of change exceeds threshold. Since the model is trained on labelled sequences of the monitored features, it detects the kinds of change it was trained on (virtual concept drift of those features).

Usage

dfr_indid(model, threshold = 0.5, target_feat = NULL, horizon = NULL)

Arguments

model

A trained indid object.

threshold

Alarm threshold on the probability of change.

target_feat

Names of the columns fed to the model, in the order of training. NULL (the default) uses the model's feature names, or every numeric column when the model has none.

horizon

If set, the state of the network is reset every horizon observations, so that the stream is read as consecutive sequences of the training length (model$seq_len is a natural choice). NULL (default) never resets it except after a drift.

Value

dfr_indid object. After fit(), drifter_output holds the probability of change of every observation (probability).

Details

After a drift the state of the network is reset, so the data after the change are read as the start of a new sequence. The model has learned what the beginning of a sequence without change looks like, so it keeps raising alarms if the new regime does not resemble it. Rows with missing values are skipped.

References

Romanenkova, E., Stepikin, A., Morozov, M. and Zaytsev, A. (2022). InDiD: Instant disorder detection via a principled neural network. Proceedings of the 30th ACM International Conference on Multimedia, 3152-3162. doi:10.1145/3503161.3548182

Examples

library(daltoolbox)
library(heimdall)
set.seed(1)
make <- function(n) {
  change <- sample(2:32, n, replace = TRUE)
  change[seq_len(n / 2)] <- 33
  x <- t(vapply(change, function(c) stats::rnorm(32, ifelse(seq_len(32) < c, 1, 6)), numeric(32)))
  labels <- t(vapply(change, function(c) (seq_len(32) >= c) * 1, numeric(32)))
  list(x = x, labels = labels)
}
train <- make(200)
model <- indid(train$x, train$labels, T = 8, learning_rate = 0.02, epochs = 30, seed = 1)
stream <- data.frame(value = c(stats::rnorm(20, 1), stats::rnorm(10, 6)))
detector <- fit(dfr_indid(model), stream)
which(detector$drifter_output$probability > 0.5)[1]
#> [1] 21
